turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Sure! First, look at one example.
I work. She works.
After "she", I add -s to "work".
So after he, she or it, the verb gets -s.
Right: He reads at night. Wrong: He read at night.

Now you try. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
turns.judgeInput:

W1 (wrong) strength 1: the verb does not change after he/she/it. Its error: leaves the verb unchanged after he/she/it ("She like tea").
W2 (wrong) strength 3: -s goes on every verb and -es/-ies are not needed. Its error: adds -s wrongly or misspells -es/-ies ("She watchs TV", "I plays").
C1 (correct) strength 0: add -s/-es after he/she/it. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
